sentence: A 47-year-old patient with a history of gastric ulcer, smoker of 10 cigarettes/day, vasectomized, who consulted for a moderate increase in left scrotal volume for years but with an increase during the last month, accompanied by dull discomfort, without acute pain.
The physical examination highlights the presence of a medium-sized hydrocele that prevents exploration of the testicle and epididymis.
General blood and urine tests were normal.
A scrotal ultrasound was performed, reporting a left intratesticular nodular image with well-defined borders, suggestive of testicular neoplasia and hydrocele with anechoic content.
A left inguinal orchiectomy was performed with placement of a silicone testicular prosthesis.
After a normal immediate postoperative period, an abdominal CT scan was performed, which was normal.

The surgical specimen macroscopically showed an infarcted area of ​​testicle alternating with another apparently normal area, confirming the presence of testicular infarction in the microscopic study with the absence of tumor.
